criteria.note: Imported policy_check and exercised ready_boundary_violations() on a temp ROOT: a spec at status:draft that carries a proof manifest is flagged; the same spec at status:ready and at status:shipped is not. Trailing-whitespace 'draft   ' is still flagged (front-matter strips). Sneak attempts do not pass a real draft: the only evasion is a non-'draft' status string (e.g. capitalized 'Status:'), which validate.check_spec independently rejects (status must be lowercase and in SPEC_STATUSES). Real-repo ready_boundary_violations()==[]; WARP-0109 spec is status:ready (not draft).

spec_revision_stale() flags proof@rev1 vs spec@rev2 and clears at rev1==rev1 and rev2>=rev2. Non-integer spec revision fails closed: a string ('two') and a float-string ('1.5') both mark the spec stale via the except (ValueError, TypeError) branch. Missing spec revision defaults to 1 (not flagged for proof@1). Missing proof spec_revision is skipped (pr is None) so prior W1..W8 proofs remain valid (back-compat). Real-repo spec_revision_stale()==[]; the W9 manifest carries no spec_revision, so its own proof is never stale.

Independently recomputed proof_digest(proof/WARP-0109/manifest.json) with a standalone script (not their code) = sha256:62bc7b1eb0fe78ae, equal to both policy_check.proof_digest and validate.proof_digest and to the task's expected value. valid_verdict_for accepts a verdict whose proof_digest matches the current manifest, rejects a mismatched digest, and (back-compat) does NOT reject a verdict carrying no proof_digest. Tampering the manifest content invalidates a verdict pinned to the old digest (no reuse). Drift-guard: the two functions produced identical output over 2000 varied inputs and the real manifest; they are functionally identical.

_approval_covers: exact named path covered, a/** glob covered, unnamed path not covered, empty and missing scope.paths cover nothing. valid_approval_for path-scoped accepts a covered path, rejects an uncovered path, rejects an out-of-range commit, rejects an expired approval, and rejects self-approval (approver==producer). THIS ship's approval-dmitry.json covers BOTH protected paths (.warp/policy_check.py and plugin/templates/.warp/policy_check.py), approver 'dmitry' != manifest producer 'claude-fable-5 (implementing agent)'. Removing .warp/policy_check.py from a copy of the scope makes valid_approval_for return None for that path (push would block) while the still-named path stays allowed. No exact protected-path approval leaks onto any of the other 6 protected paths.

findings.text: Drift-guard is a single-input functional equality assertion in selftest, not a source/AST identity check. The two proof_digest functions are functionally identical today (verified over 2000 varied inputs + the real manifest) but are NOT byte-identical in source: policy_check uses hashlib.sha256 while validate uses the _hashlib alias, and the docstrings differ. The manifest AC3 note 'Digest fn is byte-identical' is imprecise (the '(template-sync md5 equal)' equality it cites is file-vs-its-template, not policy_check-vs-validate); the spec's own AC3 wording 'identical ... drift-guarded' is satisfied functionally. Hardening: assert AST/source identity, or exercise the drift-guard with multiple vectors incl None-valued fields.

_approval_covers prefix-fallback (fnmatch(path, pat.rstrip('*')+'*')) appends '*' to EVERY entry, so a non-glob entry becomes a prefix match. A truncated/directory entry in scope.paths therefore authorizes more than it literally names (e.g. '.warp/policy' covers both .warp/policy_check.py and .warp/policy.yaml; '.warp/' covers the protected enforcer). This never fails open on absence and cannot bypass a required approval; it only broadens an already-present, self-separated, commit-bound, unexpired human authorization, and only when the author writes a prefix. This ship's approval names exact full paths, so no over-reach occurs here and no exact protected-path name leaks onto another protected path. Hardening: treat entries without glob metacharacters as exact matches.

ready_boundary_violations keys on lowercase front-matter 'status' == 'draft'; a mis-cased 'Status:' or any non-'draft' label evades the boundary, but validate.check_spec independently requires a lowercase status in SPEC_STATUSES, so a spec cannot ship with a mis-cased/invalid status. Belt-and-suspenders, not an exploitable bypass.

summary: Independently reproduced all four acceptance criteria by importing and exercising the actual functions in .warp/policy_check.py against temp trees, plus the real repo state. AC1 (ready-spec boundary), AC2 (spec-revision invalidation, non-integer fails closed), AC3 (verdict-proof digest binding; independently recomputed manifest digest = sha256:62bc7b1eb0fe78ae matching both functions and the task value; back-compat verdict-without-digest not rejected), and AC4 (self-separation + path-scoped authorization; this ship's approval covers both touched protected paths with approver dmitry != producer claude-fable-5) all CONFIRMED. Integrity: selftest 121 passed / 0 failed; verify.sh GATE GREEN at 224ae5f with 0 undeclared; policy_check at HEAD correctly blocks only for the not-yet-landed verdict. Once the evidence commit adds this verdict + the untracked proof dir, the push passes: verdict inherits via the parent (evidence-commit) rule, both protected paths are covered by an unexpired self-separated commit-bound approval, spec is ready (not draft), the W9 manifest carries no spec_revision (not stale), and there is no open emergency debt. Back-compat holds: all 13 existing W1..W8 verdicts carry no proof_digest and are not spuriously rejected; no existing proof is flagged by the new checks; optional fields are enforced only when present. capabilities.yaml is honest (5 new mechanical; full_contract_schemas_digests and auth-gateway identity kept absent). No em/en-dash, double-hyphen, or non-ASCII in W9's added lines; docs/plugin stay generic (only the author name appears, which is standard package metadata). Three residual hardening notes, none blocking. Verdict: pass.
